statement: For canonical grades K != J in Integer, the station lattices L_K = tau^K Z and L_J = tau^J Z satisfy L_K cap L_J = {0} by the transcendence of tau = 2pi (Lindemann 1882). For the scaled Dirichlet series F_K(s) = tau^(-Ks) zeta(s), the logarithmic derivative difference -F_K'/F_K + F_J'/F_J = (K-J) log tau is an exact constant everywhere on C, identically independent of all zeros and primes. The dilated logarithmic frequencies {tau^(-K) log n} in origin argument dilation Z_K(s) = zeta(tau^(-K) s) and translated Dirichlet frequencies {log n + K log tau} in F_K(s) are distinct constructions; scalar series preservation does not falsify every proposed non-scalar coupling involving L_K or argument dilation Z_K.
object_studied: Integer-grade station lattices L_K and transported Dirichlet series F_K(s)
fourier_normalization: Centered coordinates z = s - 1/2 = a + it; tau = 2pi
exact_conclusion: L_K cap L_J = {0} for K != J in Integer; -F_K'/F_K + F_J'/F_J == (K-J) log tau identically on C; frequency dilation and Dirichlet series translation are distinct operations
logical_negation: There exist non-zero integers m, n and distinct integer grades K != J such that m tau^K = n tau^J, or -F_K'/F_K + F_J'/F_J depends on zeros or primes (FALSIFIED)
falsification_attempts: Tested symbolic lattice non-coincidence in SymPy
Evaluated counterexample k = log_tau(2) showing real grades can collide (L_k cap L_0 = 2Z != {0})
Verified -F_K'/F_K + F_J'/F_J == (K-J)*log(tau) to 80 dps across complex points
Boundary dominance audit: as Re(s) -> infinity, F_K(s) -> tau^(-Ks) and -F_K'/F_K -> K*log(tau), exactly matching the scalar constant difference

external_sources.source: Lindemann, F. (1882), Uber die Zahl pi, Math. Ann. 20, 213-225

remaining_analytic_dependencies: Non-scalar coupling of station lattices L_K to argument-dilated zero divisor Z_K (OPEN)
